caption:
Bad visa advice: "apply wherever the appointment is fastest."

Tempting, and risky. Schengen rules say you apply to your main destination — where you will spend the most nights — or your first entry point if the split is even.

Availability, nationality and previous visa history all shape which consulate suits you. But that strategy operates inside the rule, not around it.

slides.headline: "JUST APPLY WHEREVER THE SLOT IS FASTEST."
slides.note: Appointment scarcity makes this advice sound practical. It is not the rule.

slides.body: You apply to the country where you will spend the most nights. If the nights are evenly split, you apply to your first point of entry.
slides.note: Border officers can and do question a traveller holding one country's visa while spending the whole trip in another.

slides.headline: LEGITIMATELY SHAPES THE CHOICE
items: Your actual itinerary and where the nights fall
Your nationality and how a given post reads that profile

slides.headline: THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS
slides.never: Pick a consulate purely because it has slots, with no intention of spending meaningful time in that country. It is not a shortcut — it is a mismatch between your visa and your trip.
slides.instead: Analyse the real itinerary, identify the correct post under the rule, then optimise timing and preparation within that. Strategy inside the rule, not around it.
